name: Chip supply
summary: China extends its pause on expanded rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage found
state: China's commerce ministry announced on 9 Nov a two-month extension of the waivers on its expanded export controls, keeping them suspended until 10 Jan while it negotiates with Washington (ThePrint, citing Reuters; The Star). Licensing controls on rare earths imposed in April 2025 remain in force. No TSMC or Samsung output stoppage or new controls halting a major supply chain were found as of 11 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Mainly affects electronics, carmakers and chip equipment suppliers. Tighter controls tend to show up as longer lead times and higher component prices rather than immediate shortages for consumers.
rubric_hit: Export controls on key inputs still in place (rare-earth licensing) = Watch; no major TSMC/Samsung disruption for Alert

sources.title: ThePrint (Reuters) — China extends suspension of new rare earth controls until January
The Star — China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
